findings.title: Missing re-check of cache after acquiring write lock
findings.body: In pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go GetWebAssets does a fast-path RLock read, then unconditionally takes the write Lock and reloads. It never re-checks entryPointAssetsCache after acquiring the write lock. If N goroutines miss the fast path concurrently, they queue on Lock and each reloads assets-manifest.json (and CDN) sequentially even though the first one already repopulated the cache. This is broken double-checked locking that causes thundering-herd file/network I/O in production.

findings.title: Error result overwrites last-good cache
findings.body: In pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go GetWebAssets unconditionally does entryPointAssetsCache = result before returning. If readWebAssetsFromFile/CDN fails, result is nil and err is non-nil, so a transient failure wipes a previously cached good value (notably in Dev mode where every call reloads). Callers then get nil plus error even though a valid value existed. Cache should only be updated when err == nil and result != nil.

findings.title: Exclusive lock held across blocking file/network I/O
findings.body: In pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go GetWebAssets holds entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock() (deferred unlock) across readWebAssetsFromFile and readWebAssetsFromCDN, which do disk I/O and an HTTP request. While one caller is blocked in I/O, all other callers block on the mutex, and pending writers starve new RLocks in Go's RWMutex. This serializes all web-asset lookups on slow I/O. Load outside the lock (or use singleflight) and only hold the lock to publish the result.
